proposed.explanation: Confuses private bidding with public bidding requirements; private owners have discretion to weigh non-price factors. Invents a 10% threshold that does not exist in private bidding procedures. Mistakes discretion for arbitrary selection; Owner's choice must follow rational, pre-established criteria to avoid breaching the implied obligation of fair dealing. In private competitive bidding, the Owner may consider qualifications, past performance, financial stability, and other factors in addition to price, provided the selection criteria are rational and established before bidding. Private bidders compete on multiple criteria (price, qualifications, past performance), not just lowest cost.
